problem: "The peak inverse voltage is the same as without the capacitor" is false for a half-wave rectifier, which this section explicitly covers (the half-wave ripple formula is given right above). Without C the half-wave diode blocks Vm; with C it blocks Vm (held by the capacitor) plus Vm (source swinging to the opposite peak) = 2Vm. Only full-wave circuits keep the same PIV.
fix: In a full-wave circuit the PIV is unchanged by the capacitor (Vm per diode in a bridge, 2Vm in a centre-tap circuit). In a half-wave circuit the capacitor raises the PIV from Vm to 2Vm, because the diode must block the capacitor voltage plus the reverse supply peak.

problem: The trap repeats the wrong general claim: "The diodes still block the same reverse voltage." A student who answers this way for a half-wave capacitor filter loses marks, and the chapter has already told them half-wave is in scope.
fix: "Expecting the capacitor to lower the peak inverse voltage. For full-wave circuits the PIV stays the same (Vm bridge, 2Vm centre-tap). For a half-wave circuit the capacitor actually doubles it, from Vm to 2Vm."

problem: "Ripple current is cut roughly in proportion to the reactance 2πf_r L" reads as if ripple current rises with reactance. The ripple current is the ripple voltage divided by the reactance, so it falls as the reactance grows.
fix: The ripple current falls roughly in proportion to 1/(2πf_r L): doubling the reactance (double L, or double the ripple frequency) halves the ripple current.

problem: "ripple falls by roughly 1/((2πf_r)²LC)" mixes a ratio with a voltage. 1/((2πf_r)²LC) is a plain number (the attenuation factor), not an amount of ripple.
fix: The output ripple falls to roughly 1/((2πf_r)²LC) of the ripple entering the filter; for example LC = 0.01 s² at f_r = 100 Hz gives about 1/4 of the input ripple.

problem: The curve is drawn from C = 100 µF, where the formula gives 200 V of ripple, far outside the small-ripple assumption the formula rests on; and the caption does not say the curve is for a full-wave (100 Hz) case, so a student cannot tell why 1000 µF gives 20 V and not 40 V.
fix: Start the plot near 500 µF (where ripple is a modest fraction of Vm), and write the caption as "Full-wave, 100 Hz ripple, 2 A load, f = 50 Hz: 1000 µF gives 20 V peak-to-peak, and doubling C halves the ripple."

problem: "doubling the capacitor only halves the ripple" uses "only" as if halving were a poor return, while the curve and the formula show exact proportionality, ripple ∝ 1/C. A student can read the caption as contradicting the formula.
fix: "doubling the capacitor halves the ripple, so cutting ripple by ten needs ten times the capacitance."

problem: "The load charge per cycle, Idc/f" is ambiguous in a rectifier chapter: per supply cycle the charge is Idc/f, but per ripple cycle (the cycle that sets the pulse width) it is Idc/(2f) in a full-wave circuit.
fix: Say "the charge the load takes in each ripple cycle, Idc/(2f) for full wave, is fixed by the load."
